problem: Existing memory-augmented embodied agents compress observations into textual summaries that lose fine-grained spatial/visual cues, and use a single memory representation for heterogeneous memory types; geometric cross-episode map fusion is also brittle under environment change and noise.
motivation: Real agents must reuse experience across episodes in dynamic environments without blindly trusting stale memory or relying on rigid geometric fusion. Cognitive psychology distinguishes episodic and semantic memory, suggesting different construction and retrieval strategies for each.
key_idea: Model episodic memory (retrieved by similarity and verified by MLLM visual reasoning on exploration maps to prune frontiers) and semantic memory (program-style, pseudocode-based rules extracted with decision-deviation detection) separately, in a training-free non-parametric framework.
insight: Ablations show the two memories are complementary: removing episodic memory mainly hurts exploration efficiency (GPT-4o LLM-Match×SPL 48.7→41.1), while removing semantic memory mainly hurts answer accuracy (LLM-Match 65.6→62.3), though it also lowers SPL slightly (47.2). Gains are largest on world-knowledge and functional questions, which suggests the rules help reasoning. Decoupling semantic and physical spaces and linking them only at retrieval time avoids alignment errors.
method: Semantic and physical space: HOV-SG-style SAM+CLIP region/place embeddings stored by camera pose with raw images; a LLM decomposes the instruction into target object, relative objects and relative areas to query them; the physical space is a lightweight 2D occupancy exploration map.
Retrieval-time inter-space interaction: no persistent geometric fusion; semantic and physical spaces are linked only by rendering retrieved observations' camera poses onto the occupancy grid.
Episodic memory recall: retrieve Top-K past observations by visual similarity, verify with an MLLM whether they come from nearby locations, and select the episode with the most Top-K target matches.

Visual-reasoning frontier pruning: an MLLM decides whether further exploration is needed (I_explore) using current and previous exploration maps; it keeps frontiers leading to unexplored regions if exploring, else keeps frontiers farther than d_min from retrieved landmarks.

Semantic memory (program-style rule extraction): an LLM turns execution logs into pseudocode of variables and functions; decision-deviation detection (distance to GT trajectory crossing an adaptive threshold S, 3-5 deviations) selects key steps; an MLLM outputs if-then, situation-suggestion or problem-solution rules.
Semantic memory retrieval: at test time top-K rules are retrieved by MiniLM-L6-v2 cosine similarity to the question and placed in the system prompt.
Meta memory: predefined cognitive states (exploration, target verification, target approaching, check ready to answer) that switch automatically.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (frozen, prompted); CLIP, SAM, MiniLM-L6-v2 used as feature extractors
setting.training_data: none (non-parametric); semantic memory distilled from 184 A-EQA training episodes and 36 GOAT-Bench training scenes
setting.action_space: frontier-based exploration on 2D occupancy map (frontier selection, then navigation to target)
setting.privileged: GT trajectories and GT answers from the training split are used only to build semantic memory offline; none at test time

numbers_note: The A-EQA split is not stated in the paper. The text says LLM-Match drops from 41.3 to 39.1 under Qwen, which conflicts with the table (43.1 with both, 41.6 without semantic, 39.1 without episodic).
results: With GPT-4o, HIMM reaches A-EQA LLM-Match 65.6 and LLM-Match×SPL 48.7, beating ReEXplore (58.3 / 37.3). On GOAT-Bench val-unseen it reaches SR 72.8 and SPL 56.1, against 3D-Mem's 68.9 / 48.9. With Qwen2.5-VL-7B it is second-best on A-EQA LLM-Match and best on LLM-Match×SPL, and on GOAT-Bench it has the best SR but slightly lower SPL than ReEXplore.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation on A-EQA and GOAT-Bench subsets, with no real-robot validation despite the dynamic-environment motivation.
Semantic memory extraction needs GT trajectories and answers from training data, plus a heuristic deviation threshold; the weaker Qwen backbone limits frontier-pruning quality from visual reasoning.
Relies on many MLLM calls (verification, frontier pruning, rule extraction), which adds cost and latency.
compares_to: GOAT-Bench baselines (Modular GOAT, CLIP on Wheels, SenseAct-NN)
